title: Transfer of adjunctions from étale to pro-étale finite coefficients
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p
e\ell$. Let $X,Y$ be separated schemes of finite type over $k$, and let $f:X	o Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-morphism, in the standing setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring annihilated by a power of $\ell$ (a finite admissible ring). On the small étale and pro-étale sites use the constant-$A$ module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $\Dctf$ for the full subcategories of bounded complexes with constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude: there is a finite interval containing the cohomology of the derived tensor with every degree-zero module sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes, sk-def-sfb-constructible].
Write $
u_T^*$ for the derived comparison functors [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback], assumed to restrict to equivalences
$
u_T^*:\Dctf(T_{\mathrm{ét}},A)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Dctf(T,A)$ for $T=X,Y$. Choose quasi-inverses $Q_T$ and their equivalence isomorphisms. Let $Rf_!$ be the functor of [sk-prop-sf-existence], and let $Rf^{\mathrm{ét}}_!$ be the étale compact-support functor for the same chosen compactification [def-amb-etale-compact-support], restricted to $\Dctf$. Let
$c_f:
u_Y^*Rf^{\mathrm{ét}}_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_!
u_X^*$ be the compact-support comparison on $\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$. Suppose
$G:\Dctf(Y_{\mathrm{ét}},A)	o\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$ is a right adjoint of
$Rf^{\mathrm{ét}}_!$ with counit $\varepsilon^{\mathrm{ét}}$. Then
$G^{\mathrm{pro}}=
u_X^*\circ G\circ Q_Y$ is right adjoint to
$Rf_!$ on $\Dctf(-_{\mathrm{proét}},A)$, with counit, under the equivalence identifications $Q_Y
u_Y^*N\simeq N$ and $G^{\mathrm{pro}}
u_Y^*N\simeq
u_X^*GN$,
$$\varepsilon^{\mathrm{pro}}_{
u_Y^*N}=
u_Y^*(\varepsilon^{\mathrm{ét}}_N)\circ c_f(GN)^{-1}.$$
The unique counit-preserving isomorphism identifies $G^{\mathrm{pro}}$ with the restriction to $\Dctf$ of the Brown adjoint $f^!$ of [sk-prop-sf-existence] on the localizing closures [sk-def-localizing-closure].

proof.text:
Put $E_T=\nu_T^*$ and let $\alpha_T:E_TQ_T\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$ be the chosen equivalence counit. For $M'\in\Dctf(X,A)$ and $N'\in\Dctf(Y,A)$ set $M=Q_XM'$ and $N=Q_YN'$. All objects used below are bounded, since the stated functors have the indicated $\Dctf$ domains and codomains. The full faithfulness in [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison], the assumed étale adjunction and the given $c_f$ give bijections
$$\Hom(M',E_XGN)\simeq\Hom(E_XM,E_XGN)\simeq\Hom(M,GN)\simeq\Hom(Rf^{\mathrm{ét}}_!M,N)\simeq\Hom(E_YRf^{\mathrm{ét}}_!M,E_YN)\simeq\Hom(Rf_!M',N').$$
The first map precomposes with $\alpha_X(M')$; the last sends $h$ to $\alpha_Y(N')\circ h\circ c_f(M)^{-1}\circ Rf_!(\alpha_X(M')^{-1})$. Each is natural: representing $u':M'_1\to M'_2$ by $E_XQ_Xu'$ commutes with $\alpha_X$ by its naturality, and representing $v':N'_1\to N'_2$ by $E_YQ_Yv'$ commutes with $\alpha_Y$. The two full-faithfulness bijections commute with composition; the other squares are precisely naturality of the étale adjunction and $c_f$. Thus the inverse of this chain is a natural adjunction Hom bijection for $Rf_!\dashv E_XGQ_Y$.

The counit is the image of $\mathrm{id}_{G^{\mathrm{pro}}N'}$ under the preceding chain. Using the equivalence triangle identities at $GQ_YN'$ yields
$$\varepsilon^{\mathrm{pro}}_{N'}=\alpha_Y(N')\circ E_Y(\varepsilon^{\mathrm{ét}}_{Q_YN'})\circ c_f(GQ_YN')^{-1}:Rf_!G^{\mathrm{pro}}N'\longrightarrow N'.$$
For $N'=E_YN$, identify $Q_YE_YN$ with $N$ using the inverse equivalence unit. The equivalence triangle identity and naturality of $\varepsilon^{\mathrm{ét}}$ and $c_f$ reduce the formula to
$$\varepsilon^{\mathrm{pro}}_{E_YN}=E_Y(\varepsilon^{\mathrm{ét}}_N)\circ c_f(GN)^{-1}.$$
For completeness, a natural Hom bijection gives its unit by transposing $\mathrm{id}_{Rf_!M'}$ and its counit by transposing $\mathrm{id}_{G^{\mathrm{pro}}N'}$ in the opposite direction. Naturality implies that composing these two maps in either triangle transposes an identity to itself, so bijectivity gives the two triangle identities. This is the elementary Hom-bijection definition of adjunction, with the stated counit.

Check the coefficient identification before invoking Brown restriction. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-condensed-ring-constant] the finite discrete ring $\underline A$ is the sheafified constant ring on profinite sets. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-scheme-ring-constant] with $B=A$: its input is exactly the preceding ring isomorphism, and it identifies $p_T^*\underline A$ with the sheafified constant ring on $T_{\mathrm{proét}}$. The ring in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] is the same constant ring: a continuous function $\pi_0(|U|)\to A$ has finitely many clopen fibres, whose inverse images form a disjoint open cover of $U$, on each member of which it is constant. Equal constant functions have equal values on every nonempty member; on the empty object the empty cover applies. Thus sheafifying the constant-presheaf map to this function presheaf gives an isomorphism of rings. By [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], internal modules over this ring are ordinary module sheaves with the identical underlying abelian sheaf. Applying this equivalence and its inverse degreewise preserves kernels, cokernels and hence quasi-isomorphisms; the inverse functors and their isomorphisms descend through localization. This is the termwise derived equivalence stipulated in [sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation]. Its coefficient conventions therefore agree with the item.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: restriction theorem and counit-compatible uniqueness; the ambient comparison-class formula is not needed for the item.

proof.text: The hypotheses of [sk-prop-sf-existence] hold: $p>0$, $\ell\ne p$, separated finite-type $k$-schemes and morphism, finite commutative $\ell$-primary $A$, and the fixed compactification. It gives $Rf_!\dashv f^!$ on the localizing closures, using the coefficient identification of Step 3. The first two conclusions of [sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation] say that this $f^!$ preserves $\Dctf$ and that the adjunction restricts there. In detail, [sk-def-localizing-closure] makes each closure a full ambient subcategory containing $\Dctf$. For $M',N'$ in the latter full subcategories the ambient Hom sets and the Brown Hom sets are identical. The restricted bijection thus has exactly the original Brown counit. Write $J=f^!|_{\Dctf}$.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: restriction theorem and counit-compatible uniqueness; the ambient comparison-class formula is not needed for the item.

proof.text:
Apply [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] to the functor $F=Rf_!$ and its two right adjoints $G^{\mathrm{pro}}$ (Steps 1–2) and $J$ (Step 4). The component $\gamma_{N'}:G^{\mathrm{pro}}N'\to JN'$ is the $J$-transpose of $\varepsilon^{\mathrm{pro}}_{N'}$ and satisfies
$$\varepsilon^{\mathrm{Brown}}_{N'}\circ Rf_!(\gamma_{N'})=\varepsilon^{\mathrm{pro}}_{N'}.$$
The cited statement makes these components natural, invertible and uniquely determined by this equation. This proves the unique counit-preserving identification with the Brown restriction.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q110-5bb8f0ac4 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the main-20261015 blueprint statement and both proof paragraphs, the unit sk-prop-sp-et-proet, every cited statement and the statement deps; review.md records each check. The statement is the one reviewed on 2026-10-16, not weakened: the added standing setting is exactly where the Brown f^! of sk-prop-sf-existence exists. The base-change morphism c_f uses the same chosen compactification as Rf_! and Rf^et_!. Step 3 identifies the coefficient categories (p_T^*A, the constant ring, Cont(pi0|U|,A)^#, module objects vs module sheaves) without assuming it. Step 1: I checked every map of the Hom chain (alpha_X precomposition, full faithfulness on bounded objects, the etale adjunction, c_f(M)^{-1}, alpha_Y) and its naturality. Step 2: I recomputed the counit, alpha_Y(N') o E_Y(eps_{Q_Y N'}) o c_f(G Q_Y N')^{-1}, and its reduction at N'=E_Y N. That reduction needs adjoint-equivalence data, which is the standard meaning of the statement's wording and can always be chosen; remark only, no change. Step 3: the finite-discrete condensed lemma's ring-object isomorphism is the monoidal input of the scheme lemma. The clopen-fibre cover and the empty cover give the comparison with def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules, and the internal-module equivalence is exact termwise, so it descends to derived categories. Step 4 uses only clauses 1-2 of sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation; the localizing closure is full, so the Brown counit is kept. Step 5 applies the Mathlib leaf det-sp-unique-right-adjoint with the correct direction of gamma. No cycle (read-only walk of the snapshot DAG); proof_deps equals the union of uses.
